Frontend: /profile parity — progress-card + progression-badges + view-leaderboards-button all visible in BOTH edit and view mode; progression-badge-1 click shows progression-badge-detail; profile-level-badge-edit click OK; view-leaderboards-button navigates to /leaderboards; leaderboard-my-rank + category/period/audience chips + search + row click all functional (level cat shows level names 'Rising Star (L4)' as scores, search 'stealth' → 1 row, row click → /profile/stealth); public profile /profile/auditcheckreal shows progression-badges + view-leaderboards-button; /admin/leaderboards toggle-cat-achievements off → save → GET /api/leaderboards?category=achievements returns 400, toggle back on → 200; hide auditcheckreal via lb-hide-input+lb-hide-add+lb-settings-save → 0 rows in search, unhide → 1 row restored; mobile 390x844 both /profile and /leaderboards render correctly, category chips horizontally scrollable (scrollWidth=1000 > clientWidth=366). minor.issue: When a category is toggled off and back on, its position in enabled_categories moves to the end (e.g., 'achievements' now stored last after off→on cycle). The immutable category_order field in DEFAULT_SETTINGS is preserved, but /api/admin/leaderboards/settings returns enabled_categories only, and Leaderboards.jsx iterates it in stored order — so chip position visibly changes. If a stable display order is desired, either sort enabled_categories by CATEGORIES constant when returning, or have the frontend order by category_order intersected with enabled_categories.

action_items: P3 (optional / minor): Stabilize enabled_categories order in leaderboards.py::settings_patch so toggling a category off then on preserves its original position (sort by CATEGORIES constant when persisting). Currently the chip order on /leaderboards shifts after each toggle cycle. Cosmetic only; all functionality is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: Hidden-user policy at leaderboards.py:186-190 is implemented correctly and matches the spec: hidden users are removed from public rows but the 'me' field is preserved with hidden:True + display_rank so the user retains a private-rank UX. This is a good separation of concerns and matches the founder's stated policy.

Cache invalidation on tie_breaker change (line 257-258) is correct — leaderboard_cache.delete_many({}) forces recompute with new sort. However, changing 'hidden_usernames' does NOT clear cache: hidden filtering happens at serving time (line 186-190) which is correct for hidden state changes but means the tests must call POST /refresh separately if they modified cached rows via computation-affecting fields — currently the code only invalidates on tie_breaker. Consider documenting or expanding auto-invalidation.
leaderboards.py::_compute_rows caps users at 5000 (line 74). For sites larger than ~5k real members this will silently truncate leaderboards. Acceptable for current scale but note as growth cliff.

PATCH endpoint accepts any subset of DEFAULT_SETTINGS keys but has no strict schema validation (e.g., 'public' bool, 'friends_enabled' bool). A payload with malformed types is silently coerced/passed through. Consider Pydantic model for future hardening.
GET /api/leaderboards page_size max is 50 (line 175) — no way to page > 50 for admin/moderation use. Non-blocking.
